en: Taal Volcano features a unique structure where a volcano island sits inside a lake that is located within another larger island.
Bohol's Chocolate Hills consist of exactly 1,268 perfectly cone-shaped grass-covered limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Taal Lake is the lowest lake in the Philippines, sitting at an elevation of five meters below sea level.
The critically endangered tamaraw, a dwarf water buffalo found only on Mindoro island, has distinct V-shaped horns.
Verde Island Passage in Batangas is scientifically recognized as the center of marine shorefish biodiversity on planet Earth.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for having the most perfectly symmetrical natural cone among all active volcanoes worldwide.
The Philippine tarsier has eyes that are as large as its entire brain, allowing it to see clearly in the dark.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the mountains of Ifugao by hand over 2,000 years ago without modern equipment.
The Philippine Trench plunges to a depth of over 10,500 meters, making it one of the deepest oceanic trenches globally.
Isabela is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, covering over 12,000 square kilometers in northern Luzon.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones every year because it sits directly along the Pacific typhoon belt.
